name: L10 PanoLab new-city federated temporal router confirmation source
question: Can the unchanged lexical-then-appearance router be checked on target-way/item-disjoint Caen targets using two cross-collection reference views and reciprocal three-frame queries?

selection.city_relation: City-disjoint from the Grenoble-only fresh-positive FP01/FP02 panel and absent from the four-target calibration roster.
selection.eligibility: Target way must not occur in either prior router cohort. Federated reference and query anchors must both be strict explicit-zero projections and use distinct collections.
selection.ordering: Sort eligible Caen rows by target-way ID then reference item ID and take the first two.
selection.reference_bank: Reuse the frozen federated reference anchor and fetch its exact reciprocal next item as the second reference.
selection.query_sequence: Fetch the exact reciprocal prev and next items around the frozen federated query anchor, yielding prev/anchor/next.
selection.metadata_gate: Every fetched item must preserve the anchor collection, exact provider-linked ID, reciprocal link, and strict zero-pose projection. Any failure seals the row invalid; never walk farther or substitute.
selection.prior_overlap: All five items per row must be disjoint from every prior component-router crop source item and FP01/FP02 temporal query item.
selection.pixel_boundary: The four federated anchors already exist from a prior portal-source audit but have received zero calls from this router. The six linked-neighbour pixels remain unseen at freeze. Selection uses no image, OCR, embedding, rank, score, or truth label.

materialization.anchor_policy: Reuse and hash-verify the four exact federated source panoramas.
materialization.neighbor_policy: Download exactly six provider-linked HD neighbours through .jpg.part files, atomically replace finals, and remove partials in a finally path.
materialization.overwrite: Refuse an existing selection, manifest, or output root.

claim_boundary.allowed: A metadata-frozen, new-city, target-way/item-disjoint Development source for two-reference and reciprocal three-query-frame evaluation of the unchanged router. Existing anchors are reused from an earlier portal-source audit; this is not a blind pixel source.
not_allowed: provider-disjoint, fully pixel-unseen, independent, open-world, conformal, FDR-controlled, or deployment confirmation
portal ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, user benefit, or safety
